page: Amazon Web Services m9g.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, this instance features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications detail 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-threaded capabilities alongside moderate multi-core and memory throughput. The m9g.large achieves top-tier results in single-threaded compression tasks, with gzip compression reaching 36.54 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.3 GB/sec. Memory performance is supported by a strong PassMark memory score of 2799.13, though large-block uncached read bandwidth is average at 65.44 GB/sec and write bandwidth is weaker at 25.02 GB/sec. Multi-core execution is relatively limited, as shown by a weak stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 3984.9 and a poor PassMark CPU score of 2830.96.

This instance is designed for general-purpose workloads that benefit from efficient single-core execution and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio. It is well-suited for static web serving, database operations, and Redis caching, where it demonstrates average throughput of 7.64 GB/sec and 6.5 million operations per second, respectively. However, it is less optimal for multi-threaded compute-heavy tasks or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds drop significantly. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation offer a resource-dense profile for lightweight microservices and utility workloads without the overhead of local storage.
